clue.text: Broadcast did test Martin Bashir: did watch show this once?

indicators.note: broadcast in the sense of scattered far and wide, so the letters that follow are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A TV interview by Martin Bashir is put to the test, and someone asks whether the watching public tuned in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' reads as television, fitting Martin Bashir the BBC journalist, but it signals the anagram. The definition asks whether a wristwatch would once have shown this time.
explanation.definitionFit: British Standard Time was the year-round clock setting tried in Britain from 1968 to 1971, so watches once displayed it.

clue.text: Ignore past and go

parts.note: by can mean past, as in 'drove by the house'
pass can mean go, as in 'time passes'

explanation.surface: Advice to forget what has happened and move on.
explanation.definitionFit: To bypass something is to go round it and so leave it unattended, a synonym for ignoring it.

clue.text: Pictures, a long time after one gets married

indicators.note: placed after the letters for one getting married, so the long time comes last

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
ages means a long time, as in 'I waited for ages'

explanation.surface: Wedding photos that arrive a long time after the couple tie the knot.
explanation.definitionFit: Images are pictures, whether photographs, paintings or likenesses in the mind.

clue.text: Characters upset princess with things

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means knocked over, so the letters for princess are turned upwards and read backwards

parts.note: Di, the princess of Wales, short for Diana
entities are things that exist

explanation.surface: Fictional characters upset a princess along with some objects.
explanation.definitionFit: A character in the sense of a person's distinct nature or self is their identity.

clue.text: Overexcited from honeymoon: young princess enjoyed romance, initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the opening letter of each of the five words is taken

explanation.surface: A young princess on honeymoon enjoys romance and becomes overexcited.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyper is informal for wildly excitable or overstimulated.

clue.text: Meets to talk about the affair, ultimately

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for talk is placed around the other letters

parts.note: gas is informal for idle talk or chatter
taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the final letter of affair is taken

explanation.surface: People meet up to discuss the affair.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowd gathers when it comes together, the same sense as people meeting.

clue.text: Good or bad at the start? Hurt very old head of state

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at the start means only the first letter of bad is wanted

parts.note: to ache is to hurt

explanation.surface: Questions whether a leader was good or bad from the outset, now that the elderly statesman has been hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikhail Gorbachev was the last leader of the Soviet Union, a former head of state.

clue.text: See 1 across
They run drugs over points across river

indicators.note: in a down clue over means above, so the drugs come first

parts.note: Es are ecstasy tablets

indicators.note: across means spanning, so the points are placed either side of river

parts.note: capes are headlands, points of land

explanation.surface: Smugglers run drugs across a river to various points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' puts R inside CAPES to make CAPERS. 'They run' is people who run away, not dealers.
explanation.definitionFit: Escapers are people who break free, so they run from captivity.

clue.text: See 1 across
See 27
Odd couples from Panorama meet: ciao to a basic life form

indicators.note: the words are split into letter pairs and only the first, third, fifth and seventh pairs are kept, so the even pairs go

explanation.surface: An odd couple meet on the TV show Panorama and say goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: Odd couples means the first, third, fifth and seventh letter pairs; paramecia is the plural of paramecium.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramecia are single-celled organisms, a textbook example of a simple life form.

clue.text: Loud singer out of tune at the beginning picked up by 13

indicators.note: picked up by means held by, so the scrambled letters sit inside the name

parts.note: 13 down is WELSHWOMAN, and Sian is a typical Welsh woman's name

indicators.note: at the beginning means only the first letter of tune is used
out of as in out of tune, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: a tenor is a singer

explanation.surface: A singer is out of tune from the start and is caught out by a Welsh woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 points to the answer of 13 down, a Welsh woman; Sian is a common Welsh name. out of rearranges the singer into ENTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A stentorian voice is very loud and powerful, named after Stentor, the herald in the Iliad.

clue.text: Horrible person admitting prince is a nerd

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the letter for prince goes inside

parts.note: sod is British slang for an unpleasant person

explanation.surface: A nasty man lets in a prince who turns out to be a nerd.
explanation.definitionFit: Spod is British slang for a dull, studious or socially awkward person, a near-synonym of nerd.

clue.text: He mows lawn for rolling, getting one from Barry?

indicators.note: rolling as in turning over, so the letters are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A man mows the lawn ready for rolling it flat, with help from someone called Barry.
explanation.walkthrough: Barry looks like a man's name, but it is a town in south Wales, so a woman from there is Welsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Barry is a Welsh seaside town, so a female native of it is a Welshwoman; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Prominent figure to first of royal children put up with Queen

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of royal is wanted

parts.note: ch is the dictionary abbreviation for child or children
to bear something is to put up with it
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A royal child is tolerated alongside the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A torchbearer leads a cause or movement, a figurative leading or prominent figure.

clue.text: Envious: regularly seen filling up still

indicators.note: filling up means stuffing inside, so the chosen letters go into the word for still

parts.note: still in the sense of calm, which is restful

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of seen is taken

explanation.surface: Someone envious is often seen bottling it up and keeping still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes EN, the second and fourth letters of 'seen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Resentful means bitter at another's good fortune, close in sense to envious.

clue.text: Sophisticated? Moved on

definitions.meaning: ... as in highly developed or complex
... as the past tense of advance, went forward

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone has become sophisticated, then answers that they have moved on.
explanation.definitionFit: Advanced describes technology that is complex and developed, and also means went forward.

clue.text: Disease that's spread on the skin right away

indicators.note: away means sent off, so the letter for right is removed

parts.note: epidermic means relating to the epidermis, the outer skin

explanation.surface: A rash spreading on the skin is treated as a disease straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'immediately', but it splits as R, then 'away' removing it.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemic is an outbreak of illness spreading widely through a population.

clue.text: See 26
Scraps outside of trendy meeting places

indicators.note: outside of means surrounding, so scraps wraps the word for trendy

parts.note: jots are tiny amounts, scraps
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Bits of trendy places where people meet up.
explanation.definitionFit: Joints is slang for bars or clubs, places where people gather.

clue.text: Guide to live with a cheat

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
a con is a swindle or cheat

explanation.surface: Advice on living with someone who cheats.
explanation.definitionFit: A beacon is a signal light that guides ships or travellers.

clue.text: Is Diana extremely suspicious? Does help

indicators.note: suspicious as in fishy or dodgy, signalling letters shuffled out of order

parts.note: taken as written; that the answer also runs backwards through Is Diana is a coincidence, as no reversal is signalled

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so the first and last letters of Diana are taken

explanation.surface: Wonders whether Diana is very suspicious.
explanation.definitionFit: To aid is to help, so aids stands for does help.

clue.text: Mostly note how he cheated: left to break up

indicators.note: break up means split apart, so the letter for left is inserted into the rearranged letters
cheated means falsified, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A note says how he was unfaithful and was left to split up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheated' rearranges NOTE HOW HE into ON THE WHOE, which 'to break up' splits with L.
explanation.definitionFit: On the whole is an idiom meaning generally or for the most part.

clue.text: Marry husband, having a constant desire

parts.note: an itch is a persistent craving

explanation.surface: A husband who always wants to get wed.
explanation.definitionFit: To get hitched is an idiom for marrying, so hitch is to wed.

clue.text: Fate to make love with male

parts.note: to do is to make, as in do a drawing
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Fate decrees making love with a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Doom is an ill destiny, the fate awaiting someone.

clue.text: Succeed with sex? Don't be daft!

parts.note: to come off is to succeed, as a plan comes off
it is informal for sex

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they will get lucky and is told not to be silly.
explanation.definitionFit: Come off it is a British exclamation of disbelief, telling someone to stop talking nonsense.

clue.text: Save me: Princess Di worried people with severe mood swings

indicators.note: worried in the sense of shaken about, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A worried Princess Diana cries out to be saved.
explanation.definitionFit: Manic-depressives have bipolar disorder, with swings between mania and depression.

clue.text: Claimed for building and home; it could be beside the point

definitions.text: it could be beside the point

indicators.note: building as in constructing, so the letters are reassembled into a new word

parts.note: place can mean home, as in come to my place

explanation.surface: Someone claimed something for a building and a house, though it may be irrelevant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beside the point' looks like 'irrelevant' but means literally next to the decimal point.
explanation.definitionFit: A decimal place is a digit position just after the decimal point, so it sits beside the point.

clue.text: Favouring active involvement: hard with child

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
and means together with
a son is a child

explanation.surface: Taking a strict approach to bringing up a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A hands-on approach involves direct, practical participation rather than delegating.
